messages:
sophia: quick q — the recent admission RFC left golden sample padding vague. do we want hedging calls for <1s p95 on smokebench?
raj: agree we need concretes. hedging helps tail but doubles requests if misconfigured. tradeoff: cost vs p99 risk.
emma: proposal: only hedge when seq len > 512 or runtime model variant is 'slowpath'. hedged window 200ms after primary start.
sophia: that seems reasonable. curious how it interacts with benchmark gating — can hedged runs contaminate golden latency numbers?
liam: they can. bench pipeline today records observed latencies from actual served requests. hedged retries would inflate median unless we tag them. we should tag hedged invocations as `retry.hedge` in telemetry.
raj: +1 to tagging. also add a metric `hedge_cost_multiplier` so billing/optimize can treat hedged work separately.
sophia: ok tagging + separate metrics. next: padding golden samples — when we craft a golden batch, do we pad to expected batch sizes to reproduce batching effects?
emma: we used to pad to nearest power-of-two for kernel perf, but that masked real traffic shapes. suggestion: keep original sample seq-len distribution and run additional synthetic padded runs only in `stress` stage.
liam: implementationally: loader can emit both `golden.native` and `golden.padded` traces. bench-bot: will schedule `golden.padded` on low-cost pools by default.
bench-bot: note: scheduling `golden.padded` adds ~15% GPU time on average for current slate. confirm via `bench-bot report --window 7d --tag padded`.
raj: ok make padded runs opt-in per-model via intake descriptor: `admit: { padded_smoke: true|false }`. default false.
emma: how about gating thresholds — gating should ignore `golden.padded` for latency SLOs but include them for throughput sanity checks.
sophia: yes. gating logic: 1) latency SLOs computed on `golden.native` 2) throughput/scale validated with `golden.padded` 3) hedged calls excluded from latency SLOs but recorded for tail analysis.
liam: I'll sketch the lint rules and a small PR to ingest descriptor changes. adding a sample of the descriptor in thread:
``` 
model_descriptor:
  name: example-7b
  admit:
    padded_smoke: false
    hedging_policy:
      enabled: true
      window_ms: 200
      trigger_seq_len: 512
```
raj: looks good. one more: rollback behavior if hedging causes regressions — we need a canary policy to disable hedging automatically if `hedge_cost_multiplier > 1.5` and `error_rate` increases by >0.5%.
emma: agree. add an alert for `hedge_cost_multiplier` and a soft rollback automation in rollout workflows.
sophia: great. can we try this change on 3 intake models next week? liam, can you pick the test candidates?
liam: I'll pick one slow legacy, one quantized, one with long-tail seqs. aiming for canary Friday.
sophia: thanks all. action items: liam PR for descriptor + lint, raj add metric names to schema, emma implement gating exclusions, bench-bot run padded smoke report and post results here Friday. :thumbsup:
